chunks.c1:
## samb-p01-v01 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference proves all things; world-traffic is his work — Śiva, by own will, praised. His body dawns made of relation: conquering though one, world-self, light, supreme Lord. Awaiting and dependence are no relation for the two inert — impossible; won selfhood or not, metaphor, not definition. Teaching self-obtaining to non-beings drops two-seatedness: form-fusion alone stands as relation's sense. No unbroken nearness — it misses relation; else iron bars. So the many's form-fusion: one-selfhood alone. Others say the many need no barring in oneness: things unmixed, thought joins them. No mere thought, this — past warding, like snake-error clinging to a shining. Clinging is no thing-like-shining but trailing after it: error, that shining strayed. So many-seen-as-one finds warrant — statable, told clear in recognition's path.

*Rasa: vīra (triumph) of demolition and retorsion — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: three refusals, then the opponent's verse testifying against itself. The vyabhicāri is wonder that joining was never mere thought. Śāstric triumph-relish: truth winning by the adversary's own words.*

## samb-p01-v01 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)

**Question.** Under what auspice does the inquiry into relation open?

**Premises.**
- With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference (bhedābhedātmasaṃbandhasaha).
- By whom all things are proved (sarvārthasādhitā); world-traffic (lokayātrā) is whose work (kṛtiḥ).
- Him, Śiva, by own will (svecchayā), we praise (stumaḥ).

**Inference.** Auspice: the Lord whose will works world-traffic proves all things with difference-and-non-difference-relation.


### Open
- Feminine adjectives (saha, sādhitā) lack an overt noun — implied śakti, or absolute construction; held open.
- svecchayā's agency (his will grounding relation vs our will in praising) held open; read as his (svātantrya seed).

## samb-p01-v02 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** What is relation, at the opening thesis?

**Premises.**
- Dawning (unmiṣan) by his body (vapuṣā) made of relation (mayena) through being, difference, and the rest (bhāvabhedādi).
- Conquering (jayati) though one (ekaḥ api): world-self (viśvātmā), light (prakāśaḥ), supreme Lord (parameśvaraḥ).

**Inference.** Thesis stated: relation is the Lord's dawning body-form, not an accident of things.

## samb-p01-v03 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Are awaiting or dependence the relation of inert things?

**Premises.**
- Awaiting (apekṣā) and dependence (pāratantryam) are no relation (na saṃbandhaḥ) for the two inert (jaḍātmanoḥ).
- From impossibility (asaṃbhavāt): even where selfhood is won (ātmalābhe'pi), it is metaphor (upacāraḥ), not definition (lakṣaṇā).
- Prose (p.2-3): the sprout 'awaits' the seed only by courtesy; awaiting, longing-for-the-other's-disposal, checking one's own will are will-determinations (saṃkalpaviśeṣa) — and will is consciousness's.

**Inference.** First reduction fails: awaiting-language smuggles in the conscious relatum it should supply.

## samb-p01-v04 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Is 'residing-in-two' the relation?

**Premises.**
- From stating self-obtaining of non-beings (asatām ātmalābhokteḥ), two-seatedness (dviṣṭhatā) is likewise abandoned (hīyate).
- Form-fusion alone (rūpasaṃśleṣa eva) thus stands (sthitaḥ) as relation's sense (saṃbandhārthaḥ).
- Prose (p.2): duality and mutual separateness would be relations too; 'residing-in-two' is said of the pair, not the relation — state it plainly in its own form.

**Inference.** Second reduction fails: two-seatedness describes relata, never the relation; form-fusion stands in its place.

## samb-p01-v05 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Is uninterruptedness the relation — and what positively is it?

**Premises.**
- Not uninterruptedness (na ānantaryam): it misses relation (asaṃbandhāt) — else it would hold of iron bars (ayaḥśalākayoḥ).
- Prose (p.2): distant father-son lack it, adjacent iron bars (even pervading substances) have it — neither necessary nor sufficient.
- Hence (tena): fusion (śleṣaḥ) of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood (aikātmyam eva).

**Inference.** Third reduction fails (with the iron-bars counterexample); positive thesis: relation is the many's form-fused one-selfhood.


### Open
- asaṃbandhāt parsed as 'missing relation' (the mark fails to track); the grammar also allows 'from non-relation' — sense identical.

## samb-p01-v06 — argument map

**Speaker.** Opponent (Dharmakīrtian; SP 5cd per MacCracken/Jha)

**Question.** Do the many need any unity at all?

**Premises.**
- No barring (bādhaḥ) of the many even in one's unity (ekasyaikye'pi) — they say, as others do.
- Things unmixed in themselves (amiśrāḥ svayaṃ bhāvāḥ) — thought (kalpanā) joins them (yojayati).
- Witness: Dharmakīrti's Sambandhaparīkṣā v.5cd (Jha Philosophy of Relations; MacCracken) — the opponent's proof-text, quoted against him.

**Inference.** The Buddhist position in its own voice: unmixed things, thought-joined; unity needs no seat.

## samb-p01-v07 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Is the joining only thought's fabrication?

**Premises.**
- This (etat) is no mere thought (na kalpanāmātram): it cannot be warded off (avāraṇāt).

- Prose (p.5): even your side admits error clinging to thing-shining, unuprootable by refutation.

**Inference.** Retorsion begins: unwardability proves the joining is no mere fabrication.

## samb-p01-v08 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** What makes error stick?

**Premises.**
- Clinging-to-shining (ābhāsalagnatvam) is not thing-resembling-shining (ābhāsasadṛśārthatā).
- It is following-after-shining (ābhāsānusāritvaṃ): error is just that — an erred shining (bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat).
- Prose (p.5): all errors concern resembling — but beyond resembling, errors hold by shining-clinging; else the silver-shell could not guide. Transaction-guiding seeming must follow the shining.

**Inference.** Error sticks by following shining, not resembling things: seeming that guides must trail being.

chunks.c1:
## samb-p02-v10 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — the consciousness-bodied need no forcing. The worldly one's reflection-object is the knower whose pith is difference inside non-difference's shine. One reflection's business touches no other thought, or knowers multiply. The many still reach oneness through one-word superimposition — pot-cloth says it. A second relation stands, qualifier with qualified, for helping's sake: it serves to know. Even in many, twoness holds — double-grasp-begot, like the king's horses, chariots, men. Grasp 'of king' stands one, toward its own kind; 'man' the other, sharing the master-kind's bond. 'The king's man' — thought after, in relation's field, by this; or the first two thought — all three, always. Spoken by the sixth, relation settles in the qualifier — reaching oneness with the qualified, yet keeping its own shape.

*Rasa: vīra (triumph) of fitted joinery — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: each fitting holds — twoness in manyness, oneness in twoness, shape kept in settling. The vyabhicāri is grammarian wonder that counting thinks. Joinery relished.*

chunks.argmap:
## samb-p02-v17 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** How many thinkings?

**Premises.**
- 'The king's man' (rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ iti) — this (eṣaḥ), after (paścāt), in relation's range (saṃbandhagocaraḥ).
- Is to be thought (kalpyaḥ) by this (anena); or the former two to be thought (kalpyau) — those three (trayaḥ) in every way (sarvathā).
- Prose: whole-thought after relation, or part-thoughts — three thinkings, all told.

**Inference.** Three thinkings: whole after relation, or the former two — all told.

chunks.c1:
## samb-p03-v19 — C1

**SUMMARY.** One short of the pure chief, secondaries mutually fit — the king's man, and the brahmin's. By other chiefs, other unities — relation-called of secondaries: the king's horse, man. Thus relation's course is told: intellects resting on Māyā-knowers, of varied views, driving transaction. Not deluded, though called so — all, moment by moment, grounded in endless-awareness reflection called self-awareness. Told, self-awareness-proved, unrefuted, useful — relation in recognition: full apparatus besides.

*Rasa: vīra (triumph) of sealing — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: the proof closes the way treatises close — measured, told, defended, sealed. The vyabhicāri is relief that delusion is denied without new machinery. Seal relished.*
chunks.argmap:
## samb-p03-v19 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** How do secondaries fit the chief?

**Premises.**
- With one short (ekahānyā) — by the pure (śuddhena), by the chief (pradhānena) — mutual fitness (anyānyayogitā) would be (syāt) of the secondary (guṇasya).
- As (yathā) the king's (rājñaḥ) man (puruṣaḥ), and (ca) the brahmin's.
- Prose: chief/secondary pairs measured against king/man, brahmin/[kṣatriya?].

**Inference.** Secondaries fit the chief one-short of pure: king's man, brahmin's.


### Open
- ekahānyā obscure (with-one-short? one short of what?) — held open as printed; no smoothing.

## samb-p03-v20 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** What other unity?

**Premises.**
- So (tathā) by another (anyena) chief (pradhānena) — what (yā) other (anyā) unity (ekatā), or (vā) by still another (apareṇa).
- Relation-called (saṃbandhākhyā) of the secondary (guṇasya) would be (syāt) — as (yathā) the king's horse (rājñaḥ aśvaḥ), man (puruṣaḥ).

**Inference.** Other chiefs, other unities: secondary's relation-called — king's horse, man.

## samb-p03-v22 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Are they deluded?

**Premises.**
- Not (na) — but (paraṃ): those (tāḥ), so (tathā) erred (bhrāntāḥ) though called — all (sarvāḥ) even (api)...
